editorial:
Imagine being fifteen and feeling like the whole world is against you. That is exactly where you find Mia. She lives in a rough neighborhood in England with a mom who cares more about partying than parenting. The vibe here is gritty and raw, making you feel the tension in every single scene. When a guy named Connor enters the picture as her mom's new boyfriend, everything changes. You will see Mia start to open up because he actually listens to her and treats her like a person, which is something she has never had before. 

The acting is what really sells this story. Mia is so believable that you cannot help but root for her to find a way out of her messy home life. While the movie moves a bit slow at times, the emotional payoff is huge. If you like stories about tough teens and complicated families, you should definitely check this out. You can rent it on Apple TV for a quick watch, or if you are a movie collector, adding the Blu-ray to your physical collection is the way to go for the best picture quality.
endingExplained: Things take a dark turn when Mia discovers that Connor is actually married with children. The trust she built with him is completely broken. In the final scenes, Mia realizes that the man she looked up to is just another liar. She ends up walking away from the toxic situation, showing that she has grown stronger. It is a sad ending, but it shows her finally breaking free from the people who let her down.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves raw stories about family struggles and coming-of-age dramas.
